fields.display_title: Official Review of Submission7218 by Reviewer UhZY
fields.replying_to: Replying to Mitigating Hallucination in Vision-Language Model with Depth and Spatial-aware Key-Value Refinement

fields.display_title: 1. "The paper claims a link between neighboring-key coherence and hallucination, but only shows PCA and attention trends and does not provide quantitative metrics"
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission7218 by Reviewer UhZY

fields.display_title: 2. “Since DSCR injects geometric priors, the paper should compare against alternatives such as (i) stronger vision encoders with built-in geometry and (ii) simply concatenating depth features to visual tokens instead of KV rewriting.”
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission7218 by Reviewer UhZY

fields.display_title: 3. "Figure 4(c,d) validates each component on its targeted subset but does not establish that combining both consistently outperforms either alone across the same benchmarks.”
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission7218 by Reviewer UhZY

fields.display_title: 4. “Breadth beyond hallucination-centric tasks is limited. The positive COCO captioning result is helpful, but a broader suite (e.g., additional VQA settings) would better establish that there is no negative transfer to general VL capabilities.”
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission7218 by Reviewer UhZY

fields.display_title: 5. "Since DSCR leaves VLM weights frozen, could the lack of adaptation to DSCR-refined keys limit the attainable gains? Have you tried enabling fine-tuning with DSCR active, and if so, did you observe larger improvements or any shift in preferred settings?”
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission7218 by Reviewer UhZY

fields.display_title: 6. "DSCR modifies only the visual branch of VLMs. Can it mitigate hallucinations that arise when the language model misinterprets visual tokens? Do you have controlled analyses or case studies indicating whether DSCR helps in such language model-driven error modes?”
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission7218 by Reviewer UhZY

fields.display_title: 7.	“Semantic richness vs. key scattering. "
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission7218 by Reviewer UhZY

fields.display_title: 8. “In Figure 1(a), the non-hallucination examples show ‘X’ and ‘O’ even though there is no wrong answer, which is confusing. Also, the ‘A.’ prefix for answers can be misread as an option label.”
fields.replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Submission7218 by Reviewer UhZY
